title: AES-256-GCM hardware accelerator
objective: Explore hardware implementations of AES-256-GCM and identify Pareto-efficient designs under explicit technology, throughput, latency, area, power, and security constraints.

scope.primary_claim: A candidate hardware implementation correctly performs the selected AES-256-GCM profile and its measured cost/performance/security properties are reproducible for a stated target.
included: AES-256 block cipher and key expansion
GCM counter mode and GHASH authentication
cycle-accurate RTL simulation and differential testing
synthesis and target-specific implementation when available
software, RTL, and optional ISA-extension baselines
constant-latency and key-lifecycle analysis where claimed
excluded: a global claim of the world's most optimized design without a target and objective function
physical side-channel resistance claims from functional simulation alone
nonce generation or protocol-level nonce management unless explicitly included as a separate block
substituting AES-GCM test vectors for security certification
scope.completion_boundary: Simulation-complete means the specified algorithm profile passes independent known-answer, edge-case, randomized, and interface tests on synthesizable RTL with reproducible measurements. Physical completion requires target implementation and, for security claims, separately appropriate leakage or fault evidence.

allowed_strategies: iterative, partially unrolled, or fully unrolled AES round datapaths
serial, folded, pipelined, or parallel GHASH multiplier structures
shared AES/GHASH datapaths or dedicated parallel units
precomputed or on-the-fly AES-256 key expansion
scalar or vector RISC-V cryptography-extension comparisons
different interface widths, buffering, DMA, and backpressure policies
non_requirements: a particular CPU, bus, interface, clock, FPGA, or ASIC library before the target profile is frozen
maximum throughput at any area or power cost
side-channel resistance beyond the explicitly measured claim
support for algorithms or AES key sizes outside the selected profile
invariants: AES-256 means a 256-bit key and the FIPS 197 AES-256 variant
GCM semantics follow the pinned SP 800-38D profile
byte ordering, bit ordering, tag ordering, IV handling, and interface framing are explicit
invalid authentication tags are never reported as successful decryption
unknown or unmeasured metrics remain null or unavailable
a security property is not inferred from functional correctness

normative_specifications: NIST SP 800-38D (GCM and GMAC; revision notice must be checked before freezing a conformance profile)
reference.oracle: independent constant-reviewed software reference plus pinned NIST/ACVP-compatible vectors
profile_freeze_requirements: supported IV lengths, including the 96-bit fast path and non-96-bit handling
supported tag lengths and truncation policy
maximum message, AAD, and invocation lengths
tag-failure output policy and key/temporary-state clearing policy

workloads.source: FIPS 197 examples and a pinned AES validation corpus
workloads.description: AES-256 encryption, decryption, and key-expansion known-answer tests, including round and intermediate checks where available.

workloads.source: NIST SP 800-38D examples and NIST ACVP AES-GCM corpus
workloads.description: Complete AES-256-GCM encrypt/decrypt vectors covering plaintext, AAD, IV, tag, and failure behavior.

workloads.source: derived fixed vectors with a recorded generation seed and profile
workloads.description: Empty and partial plaintext/AAD, one-byte and block-boundary lengths, non-96-bit IVs, tag lengths, backpressure, reset, and tag rejection.
workloads.comparison: exact outputs plus explicit protocol-state assertions

workloads.source: pinned deterministic generator seed and independent software reference
workloads.description: Randomized keys, IVs, AAD, plaintext, lengths, and valid/invalid tags, with reproducible vector archives.
workloads.comparison: all vectors and negative cases must agree

workloads.source: fixed workload matrix generated from the frozen profile
workloads.description: Cold and warm key paths, message sizes from sub-block to large streaming buffers, AAD ratios, and sustained streams.
workloads.comparison: cycles, latency, throughput, and resource-normalized metrics

workloads.description: Arbitrary input/output stalls, packet boundaries, simultaneous channels, reset at legal and illegal phases, and FIFO pressure.
workloads.comparison: scoreboard plus protocol assertions; no dropped, duplicated, or reordered bytes

workloads.source: RTL inspection, assertions, trace analysis, and later physical tests
workloads.description: Data-independent control/latency review, key zeroization, tag-failure behavior, fault response, and side-channel plan.
workloads.comparison: claim-specific evidence; simulation alone cannot certify leakage resistance

requirements: AES-256 block encryption/decryption and key schedule agree with the independent oracle
GCM ciphertext and tag agree for all positive vectors
invalid or modified tags are rejected for all negative vectors
empty, partial, and block-aligned messages behave according to the selected profile
96-bit and supported non-96-bit IV processing are distinguished and tested
AAD affects authentication but is not included in ciphertext
stream stalls do not alter outputs or internal message boundaries
reset and key changes do not leak prior message state into a later operation
forbidden_shortcuts: using a host crypto library in place of candidate RTL during the measured run
reading expected ciphertext, tags, or result verdicts from the oracle inside the candidate
accepting a tag mismatch as a successful decrypt or releasing unauthenticated plaintext contrary to the frozen policy
reporting area, timing, power, or security values that were not measured
calling a functionally correct implementation constant-time without latency/control evidence
comparing designs with different workload, target, compiler, clock, or amortization assumptions without labeling the difference
correctness.unknown_policy: If a target tool, power model, side-channel instrument, or physical board is unavailable, record the metric as null/unavailable and keep the claim limited to what was measured.

metrics.meaning: All selected positive and negative vectors pass exact comparison.
Cycles from accepted key/IV/message start to first valid result, with cold/warm key paths separated.
Sustained authenticated-data throughput under a stated clock and interface width.
Amortized and non-amortized values for each message-size class.
LUT/FF/BRAM/DSP or ASIC cell/area result for a named tool, library, and constraint set.
Post-synthesis or post-route timing for a named target.
Measured or tool-estimated only, with method and confidence recorded.
Constant-latency, zeroization, fault, or leakage evidence is reported separately rather than collapsed into correctness.

criteria: normative AES and GCM revisions are pinned
byte/bit order, IV, tag, length, reset, and tag-failure semantics are documented
target profile and objective function are explicit
primitive, full-GCM, edge, random, and interface workloads pass
synthesizable RTL lint and synthesis pass
candidate never calls host crypto or reads oracle verdicts
cycle and throughput measurements are reproducible for frozen vectors
all unknown metrics and security limitations are labeled
named FPGA or ASIC target accepts the exact RTL configuration
timing constraints and resource reports are retained
physical output matches RTL for the same vectors
each security claim has a stated threat model
data-dependent control and latency paths are inspected or asserted
physical leakage/fault claims use appropriate measurements rather than simulation-only inference

exit_criteria: profile is frozen and normative sources are recorded
independent reference and vector generator agree on pinned fixtures
portable software and first synthesizable RTL baselines pass all primitive and GCM correctness tests
interface and vector formats are stable
at least two materially different hardware organizations are measured under the same profile
results are compared as a Pareto set or against an explicitly justified weighted objective
all simulation-complete gate criteria pass from a clean committed revision
target-implemented gate passes for an available FPGA or ASIC flow
security claims are either supported by claim-appropriate evidence or explicitly withdrawn

artifact_layout.candidate: workspace/ or a future experiment-specific candidate directory
artifact_layout.vectors: experiment run artifacts; committed only when licensing and size are appropriate

provenance_requirements: experiment profile revision and normative source URLs/revisions
candidate RTL/firmware commit and exact interface configuration
vector corpus seed, generator version, corpus hash, and reference implementation identity
model canonical ID/alias, harness version, reasoning effort/mode, prompt/instruction hashes
agent, human, build, simulation, synthesis, and physical time separately
target, clock, constraints, compiler flags, synthesis/P&R tool versions, and rate/cost sources
all correctness, performance, area, timing, power, and security artifacts

research.title: NIST FIPS 197, Advanced Encryption Standard
research.fact: Defines AES-128, AES-192, and AES-256 over 128-bit blocks; the 2023 update made editorial changes without changing the algorithm.

research.title: NIST SP 800-38D, GCM and GMAC
research.fact: Defines GCM authenticated encryption and GMAC; NIST has announced that the publication is being revised, so the chosen revision must be recorded.

research.title: NIST Automated Cryptographic Validation Protocol
research.fact: Provides a machine-oriented validation protocol and AES-GCM materials suitable for a pinned vector and response contract.

research.title: RISC-V scalar cryptography specification
research.fact: Provides a standards-based optional comparison point for scalar AES-related hardware instructions and data-independent timing requirements.

research.title: RISC-V vector cryptography specification
research.fact: Defines vector AES and GHASH-related extensions that can inform an optional vector-accelerated comparison, not a mandatory architecture.

current_baseline.available_host_support: Verilator and Yosys are present; no FPGA/ASIC implementation flow or physical board is currently detected.
current_baseline.next_decision: Freeze the algorithm/interface/target profile before implementing a hardware candidate.
